items.Sentence: Raw sewage first enters the septage receiving station where it's mixed with air in the septage holding tanks. The raw sewage is then received at the headworks, where it's passed through a grit chamber to separate solid particles.

Wastewater is then mixed with activated sludge in the mixed liquor structure, and it is subsequently directed to a 170 feet (ft) x 124 ft Biolac® aeration basin where air is once again introduced into the sewage water.
Wastewater discharged from the Biolac® aeration basin is then passed through two (2) secondary clarifiers (40 ft x 43 ft) in parallel.

Sludge collected from the secondary clarifiers is dewatered at a rotary drum thickener and then pumped to six (6) sludge drying beds (three (3) sludge beds measuring 70 ft x 38 ft and three (3) more measuring 92 ft x 40 ft). The sludge drying beds are equipped with sand filters and perforated underdrains.
The wastewater from the secondary clarifiers flows through a ultraviolet (UV) disinfection system and an effluent flow metering system before being discharged to the Pear Drain.
